fullPassage:
Did you know that February 2nd is World Wetlands Day? Some may wonder whether wetlands are important enough to celebrate every year. They may think wetlands are useless and unpleasant places, but actually they are unique ecosystems that must be protected because they provide numerous benefits to both the environment and humans. For example, Upo is Korea's largest untouched wetland, covering an area as big as 210 soccer fields. First of all, Upo is a habitat for a number of threatened and endangered species. To name a few, there is the rare gasiyeon and the ttaogi, a bird which is nearly extinct. Furthermore, Upo prevents floods by absorbing water during the rainy season of July and August, and it supplies adequate water to local farmers during droughts. Like Upo, there are other wetlands in the world that help the environment and humans around them. Let's take a look at some of them.

The Camargue / France
The Camargue is a region in southern France where the Rhône River meets the Mediterranean Sea, just a few miles from the city of Arles. It functions as a natural sponge, absorbing and gradually releasing surface water such as rain, groundwater, and floodwater. Its ability to hold water aids in flood control. The Camargue is also an excellent place to observe more than 400 species of birds. Due to the fact that wetlands and lakes cover 35% of the area, the Camargue is an ideal place for flocks of birds to feed and cool off. The exotic pink flamingo is one of the most famous species found there. The area is also known historically for its white horses. The Camargue horses are a special breed, said to be one of the world's oldest, and they have spent thousands of years living in the unique environment of the Camargue and adapted to its salty wetlands. They have become powerful and strong as a result of surviving in the Camargue, where only reeds, thick grasses, and weeds are available. If you have ever seen a magnificent image of horses running through water, it is very likely that they are Camargue horses from this area.

The Everglades / USA
The Everglades is a wetland that stretches from Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. It functions as a "biological supermarket." Many birds and mammal species rely on the Everglades for food, water, and shelter, particularly during the migration and breeding seasons. For example, the Florida panther has flourished in the Everglades. It was nearly extinct in 1995, with only a dozen adults estimated in the wild. But the whole population in the Everglades National Park had recovered to about 230 by 2017.

What is more, the Everglades is the only place where American crocodiles and American alligators coexist. These animals typically inhabit different ecosystems: crocodiles live in salt water, whereas alligators live in fresh water. However, they are found living together where fresh water from Lake Okeechobee meets the salt water of Florida Bay. Besides, the Everglades provides drinking water to people in Florida, with one out of every three people relying on the Everglades for drinking water. Unless the Everglades is preserved, millions of people will suffer from a shortage of drinking water.

The Sudd / South Sudan
The Sudd wetland is the largest wetland in Africa, sustained by the flow of the White Nile from Lake Victoria in Uganda. In the Sudd, there are many endangered mammal species, including African elephants and antelopes. Additionally, one million people rely on the wetland for a living, primarily through cattle herding. For example, during the dry season, nomadic people move deeper into the wetland and build seasonal homes on naturally occurring islands to feed their herds like sheep, cows, and goats and catch the abundant fish. The name "Sudd" comes from an Arabic word for "barriers," and the wetland historically protected the people from invaders. The Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans spent centuries searching for the starting point of the Nile River. Nero, the emperor of the Roman empire, sent the military to explore the White Nile in 61 AD, but his soldiers were unable to proceed beyond the Sudd.

Wetlands, no matter where they are found, clearly provide habitats for a variety of endangered plant and animal species, as well as humans. Unfortunately, wetlands are currently under threat. The Camargue, for example, is decreasing as sea levels rise due to climate change. The Everglades used to be much larger, but due to agriculture and urban development, less than half of the historic Everglades remains today. The Sudd has been contaminated by oil spills from oil extraction activities. It is estimated that 64% of the world's wetlands have disappeared. Now that we understand the importance of wetlands in maintaining our ecosystems, we should consider ways to live without destroying the wetlands that provide valuable benefits to animals, plants, and humans.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ absorb → absorbing: 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① numerous: 형용사로 benefits를 수식 — 적절.

✅ ② covering: 분사구문(= and it covers) — 적절.

✅ ③ threatened: 과거분사(위협받는) — 수동 의미 적절.

❌ ④ absorb → absorbing: 'by + V-ing' 구조. 전치사 뒤에 동사원형 불가. ←정답
det.tip: 전치사 + V-ing: by absorbing, in making 등. 전치사 뒤 동사원형 절대 불가.

det.korean: ① which → where: 장소(a region in southern France)를 선행사로 하므로 관계부사 where가 필요하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① which → where: 'a region in southern France'라는 장소 선행사 + 뒤에 완전한 절(the Rhône River meets ~)이므로 관계부사 where가 필요. ←정답

✅ ③ surviving: 'as a result of + V-ing' 전치사 뒤 동명사 — 적절.

det.tip: 관계대명사 vs 관계부사: 선행사가 장소이고 뒤에 완전한 절 → where. which 뒤에는 불완전한 절(주어/목적어 빠진 절).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ which → where: 장소(the only place)를 선행사로 하므로 관계부사 where가 필요.
det.analysis:
✅ ① rely: 복수주어(species) + rely — 수 일치 적절.

✅ ② estimated: 'with + O + p.p.' — adults가 추정의 대상(수동) — 적절.

❌ ③ which → where: 'the only place'(장소 선행사) + 뒤에 완전한 절(crocodiles and alligators coexist) → 관계부사 where 필요. ←정답

✅ ④ is preserved: Unless + 수동태(보존되다) — 적절.
det.tip: place/area/region → where(장소 관계부사). the only place where ~ coexist. which 뒤에는 불완전한 절.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ fragile(허약한) → strong(강한): 혹독한 환경에서 생존하여 '강해졌다'가 적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ① excellent(훌륭한): 400종 이상 관찰 가능한 장소 — 원문 일치.
→ 본문: 'an excellent place to observe more than 400 species'.

✅ ② exotic(이국적인): 핑크 플라밍고의 특성 — 원문 일치.
→ 본문: 'The exotic pink flamingo'.

✅ ③ white(흰색의): 카마르그의 상징적인 흰 말 — 원문 일치.
→ 본문: 'known historically for its white horses'.

❌ ④ fragile(허약한) → strong(강한): 'powerful and strong as a result of surviving' — 혹독한 환경 생존 결과. ←정답
det.tip: powerful and strong(강력하고 강한): 혹독한 환경에서 생존한 결과. fragile(허약한)은 반대.

questions.passage: The Everglades provides drinking water to people in Florida, with one out of every three people relying on the Everglades for drinking water. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ expanded(확장되었다) → disappeared(사라졌다): 습지가 위협받고 사라지고 있다는 부정적 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ① preserved(보존되다): 보존되지 않으면 고통 — 원문 일치.
→ 본문: 'Unless the Everglades is preserved'.

✅ ② threat(위협): 습지가 위협받고 있다 — 원문 일치.
→ 본문: 'currently under threat'.

✅ ③ contaminated(오염된): 석유 유출로 오염 — 원문 일치.
→ 본문: 'contaminated by oil spills'.

❌ ④ expanded(확장되었다) → disappeared(사라졌다): 64%가 사라졌다는 위기 상황. 확장은 반대 의미. ←정답
det.tip: disappeared(사라졌다) ↔ expanded(확장되었다). 습지 64% 소실 = 위기.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 카마르그는 물을 흡수하고 서서히 방출하는(absorbing and gradually releasing) 스펀지 역할을 한다.

❌ ① distributing and storing(분배하고 저장하는): 스펀지의 기능은 분배가 아닌 흡수와 방출.

❌ ③ filtering and purifying(여과하고 정화하는): 걸러내는 기능이지 흡수/방출이 아님.

❌ ④ evaporating and condensing(증발시키고 응축시키는): 물의 상태 변화이지 스펀지 기능이 아님.
det.tip: absorb(흡수하다) + gradually release(서서히 방출하다) = sponge(스펀지)의 두 기능.

det.korean: 에버글레이즈는 플로리다 주민들에게 식수(drinking water)를 제공한다.

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

❌ ① '서식하지 않는다': 'habitat for threatened and endangered species' — 서식함.

→ 본문: 따오기는 거의 멸종. ←정답: ③

❌ ③ 일치: 'stretches from Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay'.
→ 본문 정확히 일치.

→ 본문 정확히 일치.
det.tip: 숫자/시기 교차 변조: 1995년 = 12마리(a dozen), 2017년 = 230마리. 순서 뒤바꿈 주의.

The History of Wildlife Conservation in Florida
Comparing Wetland Ecosystems Across North America

det.korean: 제목: 에버글레이즈 — 야생동물과 인간에게 필수적인 생태계.
det.analysis:
✅ ① The Everglades: A Vital Ecosystem for Wildlife and Humans
(에버글레이즈: 야생동물과 인간에게 필수적인 생태계)
→ 근거: biological supermarket(야생동물) + drinking water(인간). 글 전체를 포괄.

❌ ② How Crocodiles Have Adapted to Freshwater Environments
(악어가 담수 환경에 적응한 방법)
→ 본문: adapt 미언급. coexist(공존)이지 adapt(적응)이 아님.

❌ ③ The History of Wildlife Conservation in Florida
(플로리다 야생동물 보전의 역사)
→ 본문: 역사적 보전 과정 미언급.

❌ ④ Comparing Wetland Ecosystems Across North America
(북미 습지 생태계 비교)
→ 본문: 비교가 아닌 에버글레이즈 한 곳 소개. ←정답: ①
det.tip: 제목은 글 전체를 포괄하는 간결한 표현. vital = 필수적인.

questions.passage: The Everglades is a wetland that stretches from Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. It functions as a "<u>biological supermarket</u>." Many birds and mammal species rely on the Everglades for food, water, and shelter, particularly during the migration and breeding seasons. The Florida panther has flourished in the Everglades. The Everglades is the only place where American crocodiles and American alligators coexist. The Everglades provides drinking water to people in Florida.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 밑줄 친 'biological supermarket'이 함축하는 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: a place where biological research is commercially funded
a rich ecosystem that abundantly provides essential resources to diverse species
a location where tourists can purchase rare wildlife products
a facility that processes and distributes natural food resources

det.korean: '생물학적 슈퍼마켓' = 다양한 종에게 필수 자원을 풍부하게 제공하는 생태계.
det.analysis:
❌ ① a place where biological research is commercially funded
(생물학 연구가 상업적으로 자금 지원되는 곳)
→ 본문: 연구/상업 미언급.

✅ ② a rich ecosystem that abundantly provides essential resources to diverse species
(다양한 종에게 필수 자원을 풍부하게 제공하는 풍요로운 생태계)
→ 근거: food, water, shelter 제공 + 다양한 종(birds, mammals, panther, crocodiles, alligators) + 인간(drinking water). 슈퍼마켓=다양한 물건 제공. ←정답

❌ ③ a location where tourists can purchase rare wildlife products
(관광객이 희귀 야생 제품을 구입하는 장소)
→ 본문: 관광/구매 미언급.

❌ ④ a facility that processes and distributes natural food resources
(자연 식품 자원을 가공/유통하는 시설)
→ 본문: 가공/유통 미언급. 자연 제공.
det.tip: 비유 해석: supermarket = 다양한 물건을 구비한 곳. biological supermarket = 생물에게 필요한 모든 것(먹이, 물, 은신처)을 제공하는 곳.

questions.passage: The Camargue is also an excellent place to observe more than 400 species of birds. The exotic pink flamingo is one of the most famous species found there. The area is also known historically for its white horses. The Camargue horses are a special breed, said to be one of the world's oldest, and they have spent thousands of years living in the unique environment of the Camargue and adapted to its salty wetlands. They have become powerful and strong as a result of surviving in the Camargue, where only reeds, thick grasses, and weeds are available. If you have ever seen a magnificent image of horses running through water, it is very likely that <u>they</u> are Camargue horses from this area.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 밑줄 친 'they'가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 물 속을 달리는 이미지 속 말들

det.korean: 'they'는 물 속을 달리는 이미지 속 말들(the horses in the image)을 가리킨다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 갈대와 풀들: 식물이 달릴 수 없음.
→ 문맥상 horses가 주어.

❌ ② 이미지를 본 사람들: 'you(당신)'가 본 사람이지 they가 아님.
→ you have seen → they are horses.

✅ ③ 물 속을 달리는 이미지 속 말들: 'horses running through water' → 그 말들(they)이 카마르그 말이다.
→ 본문: 'it is very likely that they are Camargue horses'. ←정답

❌ ④ 카마르그 습지의 야생 동물들: 이미지 속 '말'을 구체적으로 지칭.
→ 동물 전체가 아닌 말(horses).
det.tip: 지칭 추론: 'a magnificent image of horses running' → they = those horses.

questions.passage: Upo is Korea's largest untouched wetland, covering an area as big as 210 soccer fields. First of all, Upo is a habitat for a number of threatened and endangered species. Furthermore, Upo prevents floods by absorbing water during the rainy season of July and August, and it supplies adequate water to local farmers during droughts. Like Upo, there are other wetlands in the world that help the environment and humans around <u>them</u>. Let's take a look at some of them.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 밑줄 친 'them'이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 'them'은 습지들(the wetlands)을 가리킨다. '습지 주변의 환경과 인간을 돕는다'는 의미.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 사람들: humans는 around them에서 도움을 받는 대상이지 them 자체가 아님.
→ 'help humans around them' = 습지 주변의 인간을 돕다.

❌ ② 멸종위기종들: 앞 문장(Upo) 맥락이지 이 문장의 them이 아님.

✅ ③ 습지들(the wetlands): 'other wetlands that help the environment and humans around them(=the wetlands)'
→ 본문: them = other wetlands. 습지 주변(around)의 환경과 인간. ←정답

❌ ④ 환경 문제들: 문맥에 없는 개념.
det.tip: 'around them' = 그것들(습지) 주변의. them = the wetlands.

questions.passage: The Sudd wetland is the largest wetland in Africa, sustained by the flow of the White Nile from Lake Victoria in Uganda. In the Sudd, there are many endangered mammal species, including African elephants and antelopes. Additionally, one million people rely on the wetland for a living, primarily through cattle herding. For example, during the dry season, nomadic people move deeper into the wetland and build seasonal homes on naturally occurring islands to feed their herds like sheep, cows, and goats and catch the abundant fish. The name "Sudd" comes from an Arabic word for "barriers," and the wetland historically protected the people from invaders.
questions.stem:
Q: 수드 습지가 아프리카 최대 습지로 유지될 수 있는 수원과 그 출발지를 본문에서 찾아 영어로 완성하시오. (영어로) (9단어)
→ The Sudd is sustained by _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____.
questions.wa: the flow of the White Nile from Lake Victoria
accept: the flow of the White Nile from Lake Victoria
questions.ans: the flow of the White Nile from Lake Victoria

det.korean: 수드 습지는 우간다 빅토리아 호수에서 오는 백나일의 흐름(the flow of the White Nile from Lake Victoria)으로 유지된다.
det.analysis:
✅ the flow of the White Nile from Lake Victoria: 원문 'sustained by the flow of the White Nile from Lake Victoria in Uganda'.
(빅토리아 호수에서 흘러오는 백나일의 흐름에 의해 유지됨)
det.tip: sustained by = ~에 의해 유지되는. the White Nile = 백나일(나일 강 주요 지류).

questions.passage: The Camargue is a region in southern France where the Rhône River meets the Mediterranean Sea, just a few miles from the city of Arles. It functions as a natural sponge, absorbing and gradually releasing surface water such as rain, groundwater, and floodwater. Its ability to hold water aids in flood control. The Camargue is also an excellent place to observe more than 400 species of birds. Due to the fact that wetlands and lakes cover 35% of the area, the Camargue is an ideal place for flocks of birds to feed and cool off. The exotic pink flamingo is one of the most famous species found there.
questions.stem:
Q: 카마르그가 홍수 조절에 도움이 되는 능력을 본문에서 찾아 완성하시오. (영어로) (8단어)
→ Its _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____.
questions.wa: ability to hold water aids in flood control
accept: ability to hold water aids in flood control
questions.ans: ability to hold water aids in flood control

det.korean: 카마르그의 물을 보유하는 능력이 홍수 조절에 도움(ability to hold water aids in flood control)이 된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ability to hold water aids in flood control: 원문 'Its ability to hold water aids in flood control.'.
→ 물 보유 능력(ability to hold water) + 홍수 조절에 도움(aids in flood control).
det.tip: ability to V = V하는 능력. aid in ~ = ~에 도움이 되다. flood control = 홍수 조절.

questions.passage: The Camargue is a region in southern France where the Rhône River meets the Mediterranean Sea. The Camargue is also an excellent place to observe more than 400 species of birds. The area is also known historically for its white horses. The Camargue horses are a special breed, said to be one of the world's oldest, and they have spent thousands of years living in the unique environment of the Camargue and adapted to its salty wetlands. They have become powerful and strong as a result of surviving in the Camargue, where only reeds, thick grasses, and weeds are available. If you have ever seen a magnificent image of horses running through water, it is very likely that they are Camargue horses from this area.
questions.stem:
위 글에서, 카마르그 말이 수천 년간 살아온 환경에 대한 설명을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (영어로) (8단어)
→ They have spent thousands of years living in _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____.
questions.wa: the unique environment of the Camargue and adapted
accept: the unique environment of the Camargue and adapted
questions.ans: the unique environment of the Camargue and adapted

det.korean: 카마르그의 독특한 환경에서 살며 짠 습지에 적응(the unique environment of the Camargue and adapted)했다.
det.analysis:
✅ the unique environment of the Camargue and adapted: 원문 'spent thousands of years living in the unique environment of the Camargue and adapted to its salty wetlands'.
→ 독특한 환경에서 생활 + 짠 습지에 적응.
(카마르그의 독특한 환경에서의 생활과 적응)
det.tip: adapt to ~ = ~에 적응하다. salty wetlands = 염분이 있는 습지.

questions.passage: The Everglades provides drinking water to people in Florida, with one out of every three people relying on the Everglades for drinking water. Unless the Everglades is preserved, millions of people will suffer from a shortage of drinking water. Unfortunately, wetlands are currently under threat. The Camargue is decreasing as sea levels rise due to climate change. The Sudd has been contaminated by oil spills from oil extraction activities. It is estimated that 64% of the world's wetlands have disappeared. Now that we understand the importance of wetlands in maintaining our ecosystems, we should consider __________.

overlay.blank: ways to live without destroying the wetlands

questions.stem:
다음 한국어 의미에 맞게 빈칸을 영작하시오. (영어로)

"습지를 파괴하지 않으면서 사는 방법을 고려해야 한다."
→ we should consider _______ _______ _______ _______ _______ _______ _______.

[조건] (1) destroying, live, the, to, ways, wetlands, without를 모두 사용 (2) (7단어)
questions.wa: ways to live without destroying the wetlands
accept: ways to live without destroying the wetlands
questions.ans: ways to live without destroying the wetlands

det.korean: 습지를 파괴하지 않으면서 사는 방법(ways to live without destroying the wetlands).
det.analysis:
ways to live without destroying the wetlands = 습지를 파괴하지 않으면서 사는 방법.

• ways to V: V하는 방법들.
• without + V-ing: ~하지 않으면서 (동시에 부정).
• destroying the wetlands: 습지를 파괴하는 것.
det.tip: without + V-ing = ~하지 않으면서. ways to V = V하는 방법.

questions.passage: The Everglades is a wetland that stretches from Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. It functions as a "biological supermarket." Many birds and mammal species rely on the Everglades for food, water, and shelter, particularly during the migration and breeding seasons. The Everglades is the only place where American crocodiles and American alligators coexist. The Everglades provides drinking water to people in Florida, with __________ relying on the Everglades for drinking water.

overlay.blank: one out of every three people

questions.stem:
다음 한국어 의미에 맞게 빈칸을 영작하시오. (영어로)

"3명 중 1명이 에버글레이즈의 식수에 의존하고 있다."
→ ... with _______ _______ _______ _______ _______ _______ relying on the Everglades for drinking water.

[조건] (1) every, of, one, out, people, three를 모두 사용 (2) (6단어)
questions.wa: one out of every three people
accept: one out of every three people
questions.ans: one out of every three people

det.korean: 3명 중 1명(one out of every three people)이 에버글레이즈 식수에 의존.
det.analysis:
one out of every three people = 3명 중 1명.

• one out of ~: ~ 중 하나.
• every three people: 모든 3명(= 3명마다).
• with + O + V-ing: 부대상황 구문.
• 전체: 3명 중 1명이 식수를 의존하고 있는 상황.
det.tip: one out of every three = 3명 중 1명. 비율 표현.
